```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"The Republican bill’s tax credits do not match the ACA’s insurance subsidies.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Many of the ten million individuals on the ACA exchanges will lose coverage.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The Republican tax credits would start at $2,000 a year for a young person.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The Republican tax credits would rise to $4,000 for those in their 50s and 60s.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The Republican tax credits will not rise with the cost of insurance.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The ACA subsidies rise with the cost of insurance.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Everyone, regardless of income up to $75,000 for individuals and $150,000 for families, receives the same amount of Republican tax credit.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The ACA’s subsidies covered almost the entire premium costs for families earning the median family income of $52,000 or below.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The ACA limited health care insurance costs to 8.5% of family total income.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Ending the ACA’s subsidies in favor of tax credits will cost 12 million people health insurance coverage, according to the CBO.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
